purpose: WebSubInterface is a Slicer module that connects Slicer to a WebSub/FHIRcast-style message hub. It can start a local hub subprocess, connect to cloud hubs, and serve the local DICOM database and scenes to browser worklist or viewer clients and to conference peers.
summary: I read the module code, CMake, the local hub launcher, the dependency installer, the hub route code I could see, and the zip extractor. Dependencies are installed only after a confirmation, at action time, with no pins on Slicer-bundled packages. The local hub binds to 127.0.0.1 with random per-run secrets. The MIT license is present. The main concern is data exposure: by default the extension connects to a third-party cloud hub run by the author. Through that hub, peers on the same topic can request the user's local DICOM worklist and images. The consent dialog is a single yes/no prompt that can be suppressed with "don't show again", and it does not say the hub is third-party. The packaging looks workable, but I could not verify it fully. There are also a few minor soundness items.
not_checked: Full contents of ImageDisplayClient.py, ConferenceDialog.py and most image_display/lib files, including how loaded remote studies are downloaded and parsed
Hub routes (oauth, conference, admin, payloads, bind_ws) and the OIDC token validation logic
Whether conference peers or topic holders are authorized before local DICOM export requests are served
Network behaviour of the author's cloud hubs (bellehumeur-engineering.com) and the SPA release assets
Build and load on an actual Slicer build; the CMake install rules and exclude patterns were reviewed by reading only
Docs, Testing/Python files and deploy scripts, except for brief searches
